question: Where can I get a list of airports in the United States, with location, operator and annual passengers, cargo and aircraft movements?

answer.summary: No single file answers it. FAA's NASR 28-day APT file lists 19,434 landing facilities (13,005 airports) with coordinates, owner name and manager name. FAA publishes CY2025 enplanements (516 commercial-service airports, 1,682 in all) and cargo landed weight (155 airports) as Excel. BTS T-100 gives 2024 passengers, departures, freight and mail for 1,279 origin codes on US-carrier domestic flights. FAA TAF gives operations by category to FY2024 for about 3,300 airports. Join on the airport identifier; definitions differ.
main_caveats: Enplanements are passenger boardings, not total passengers. FAA CY and BTS T-100 numbers for the same airport differ: ATL CY2024 52,511,402 (FAA) vs 45,406,031 (BTS 2024); ORD 38,575,693 vs 31,613,389.
BTS T-100 totals cover domestic airports served by US carriers only, by origin code; 37 of 516 FAA commercial-service airports have no matching BTS code and 343 BTS codes are not NASR airport IDs.

TAF operations are fiscal year (Oct-Sep). Towered airports are counted by controllers; at non-FAA facilities operations are estimates. FY2024 is the last actual year in the 2025 TAF; later years are forecasts.
NASR APT.txt is fixed width (230 MB); its annual operations and based-aircraft fields are declared in the layout but empty in all 19,434 records.
Airport, heliport and seaplane base share one file and one counting unit: 13,005 airports among 19,434 facilities. Terminals and runways are separate records.
ADIP and ATADS are form-driven viewers: ADIP is a JavaScript app with a login for airport users, and a scripted ATADS report request returned an empty page.
answer.confidence_reason: NASR, FAA Excel files, BTS T-100 and TAF were downloaded and joined by identifier; ADIP and ATADS were only viewed and the totals definitions across FAA and BTS stay unreconciled.

attributes.note: Airport reference point per facility: 19,434 landing facilities, 13,005 of type airport, with FAA identifier. All 13,005 airport rows carry survey method E (estimated).
NASR gives owner type, owner name (12,887 of 13,005 airports) and a manager name (a person); NTAD gives only the owner type code.
attributes.gap_note: No separate operating organisation field: the manager is a named person and the owner may be a city, authority or private party. Concessionaires and operators other than the owner are not listed.

attributes.note: Enplanements (boardings) per airport: FAA CY2025 for 516 commercial-service airports; BTS T-100 2024 adds passengers per leg. Neither is total arriving plus departing.
attributes.gap_note: Total passengers (arrivals plus departures) were not found in the files tested. Individual airport authority traffic reports were not opened.

attributes.note: FAA CY2025 landed weight in pounds for 155 cargo airports; BTS T-100 2024 freight and mail in pounds for 1,279 origin codes (US carriers, domestic flights).
attributes.gap_note: No file tested gives total cargo (international and belly included) for every airport; FAA covers 155 cargo airports and BTS covers US-carrier domestic flights only.

attributes.note: TAF operations by category (air carrier, air taxi, GA, military; itinerant and local) to FY2024 for about 3,300 airports; BTS departures and arrivals cover T-100 flights only.
attributes.gap_note: ATADS tower counts were not retrieved (report form returned an empty response to scripted requests) and the NASR operations fields are blank in every record.

steps: Download the zip from the cycle page (HEAD requests returned 503, GET worked) and extract APT.txt (230,498,814 bytes).
Read as latin-1; keep rows whose first three characters are APT; ignore RWY, ATT, RMK and ARS records.
Slice fields by the 1-based start positions and lengths in Layout_Data/apt_rf.txt; filter the facility type to AIRPORT for the 13,005 airports.
Join the identifier (cols 28-31) to the Locid of FAA enplanement and cargo files.
reading_traps: The layout declares based aircraft and annual operations (A90-A105), but cols 1005-1071 are blank in all 19,434 records.
Latitude and longitude come as formatted text (for example 41-58-36.9850N); the longitude seconds field is also in the record.
A manager name is a person; the owner name may be a city, authority, state or company.

Declared operations and based-aircraft fields are empty in every record.

open_questions: How do FAA CY enplanements, BTS T-100 and TAF enplanements relate? Observed for CY2024/FY2024: ATL 52,511,402 (FAA), 45,406,031 (BTS), 45,449,813 (TAF aac+aat+commuter); ORD 38,575,693, 31,613,389 and 31,388,080. Starting point: TAF Enplanements workbook columns us_flag and frgn_flag and the TAF glossary. Next step: read the glossary and test whether international columns close the gap.

What are the ATADS counts for towered airports? Starting point: https://aspm.faa.gov/opsnet/sys/Airport.asp (form posts to opsnet-server-x.asp; a scripted request returned an empty page). Next step: run the form in a browser-capable client and compare with TAF FY2024.

Why do 37 FAA commercial-service airports lack a BTS 2024 origin code and 343 BTS codes lack a NASR airport ID? Starting point: the unmatched lists (for example DJT, IWA, GPI, GSN). Next step: check code changes and T-100 coverage per airport.

Where are total passengers (arrivals plus departures) published per airport? Starting point: airport authority traffic reports of the large hubs. Next step: open the reports of a few hubs and compare with FAA boardings.
Why does the TAF operations workbook list 3,383 identifiers while Airports.xlsx has 3,319 rows? Starting point: the two workbooks. Next step: list the extra identifiers and read the TAF glossary.
